subject.title: [Feature]: Supports Windows 11 MSYS environment and Fishshell.

question: Should OpenClaw officially support `install.sh` under Windows MSYS2/MINGW with fish-shell PATH handling, or keep Windows installs limited to Windows Hub, PowerShell, and WSL2?
rationale: The source change is mechanically plausible, but it changes the Windows support matrix and needs real Windows shell proof before automation should choose the behavior.

options.title: Support MSYS2 and fish
options.body: Approve explicit MSYS2/MINGW handling in `scripts/install.sh`, fish PATH guidance, docs, focused installer tests, and real Windows MSYS2 smoke proof.

options.title: Document as unsupported
options.body: Keep `install.sh` scoped to macOS/Linux/WSL and update docs or diagnostics to steer MSYS2/MINGW users to WSL2, Windows Hub, or `install.ps1`.

options.title: Split fish guidance only
options.body: Allow a narrow fish PATH guidance fix while leaving MSYS2/MINGW install support for a later Windows platform decision.

recommendation.title: Support MSYS2 and fish
recommendation.body: Approve explicit MSYS2/MINGW handling in `scripts/install.sh`, fish PATH guidance, docs, focused installer tests, and real Windows MSYS2 smoke proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest current review and blame-backed routing signal for the installer/docs support boundary in this checkout.
